title: Octopus: Smart, Strange and Short-Lived
summary: Sara and George discuss the biology of octopuses, their surprising intelligence, unique anatomy, and life cycles, contrasting reality with ancient myths and cultural history.

An **octopus** (pl.: **octopuses** or **octopodes**[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Octopus#cite_note-3)) is a soft-bodied, eight-limbed [mollusc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mollusc "Mollusc") of the [order](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_(biology) "Order (biology)")**Octopoda** (, [_ok-TOP-ə-də_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Pronunciation_respelling_key "Help:Pronunciation respelling key")[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Octopus#cite_note-4)). The order consists of some 300 [species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Species "Species") and is grouped within the class [Cephalopoda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cephalopod "Cephalopod") with [squids](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Squid "Squid"), [cuttlefish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuttlefish "Cuttlefish"), and [nautiloids](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nautiloid "Nautiloid"). Like other cephalopods, an octopus is [bilaterally symmetric](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Symmetry_in_biology "Symmetry in biology") with two eyes and a [beaked](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cephalopod_beak "Cephalopod beak") mouth at the centre point of the eight limbs.[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Octopus#cite_note-6) An octopus can radically deform its shape, enabling it to squeeze through small gaps. They trail their appendages behind them as they swim backwards. The [siphon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siphon_(mollusc) "Siphon (mollusc)") is used for [respiration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aquatic_respiration "Aquatic respiration") and [locomotion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aquatic_locomotion "Aquatic locomotion") (by [water jet propulsion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jet_propulsion#Jet-propelled_animals "Jet propulsion")). Octopuses have a complex nervous system and excellent sight, and are among the most intelligent and behaviourally diverse [invertebrates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invertebrate "Invertebrate").

Octopuses inhabit various [ocean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ocean "Ocean") habitats, including [coral reefs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coral_reef "Coral reef"), [pelagic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pelagic "Pelagic") waters, and the [seabed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seabed "Seabed"); some live in the [intertidal zone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intertidal_zone "Intertidal zone") and others at [abyssal depths](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abyssal_zone "Abyssal zone"). Most species grow quickly, mature early, and are short-lived. In most species, the male uses a specially-adapted arm to deliver sperm directly into the female's mantle cavity, after which he becomes [senescent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senescent "Senescent") and dies, while the female deposits fertilised eggs in a den and cares for them until they hatch, after which she also dies. They are predators and hunt [crustaceans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crustacean "Crustacean"), [bivalves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bivalves "Bivalves"), [gastropods](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gastropod "Gastropod") and fish. Strategies to defend themselves against their own predators include expelling [ink](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cephalopod_ink "Cephalopod ink"), [camouflage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camouflage "Camouflage"), and [threat displays](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Threat_displays "Threat displays"), the ability to jet quickly through the water and hide, and deceit. All octopuses are [venomous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venom "Venom"), but only the [blue-ringed octopuses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue-ringed_octopus "Blue-ringed octopus") are known to be deadly to humans.

Octopuses appear in [mythology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mythology "Mythology") as sea monsters such as the [kraken](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kraken "Kraken") of Norway and the [Akkorokamui](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akkorokamui "Akkorokamui") of the [Ainu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ainu_people "Ainu people"), and possibly the [Gorgons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gorgons "Gorgons") of [ancient Greece](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ancient_Greece "Ancient Greece"). A battle with an octopus appears in [Victor Hugo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Hugo "Victor Hugo")'s book _[Toilers of the Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toilers\_of\_the\_Sea "Toilers of the Sea")_. Octopuses appear in Japanese _[shunga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shunga "Shunga")_ erotic art. They are eaten and considered a delicacy by humans in many parts of the world, especially the [Mediterranean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mediterranean_cuisine "Mediterranean cuisine") and Asia.

## Etymology and pluralisation

The [scientific Latin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neo-Latin "Neo-Latin") term _[octopus](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/octopus#Latin "wikt:octopus")_ was derived from [Ancient Greek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ancient_Greek "Ancient Greek")[ὀκτώπους](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/%E1%BD%80%CE%BA%CF%84%CF%8E%CF%80%CE%BF%CF%85%CF%82#Ancient_Greek "wikt:ὀκτώπους") (_oktōpous_), a [compound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Compound_(linguistics) "Compound (linguistics)") form of [ὀκτώ](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/%E1%BD%80%CE%BA%CF%84%CF%8E#Ancient_Greek "wikt:ὀκτώ") (_oktō_, 'eight') and [πούς](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/%CF%80%CE%BF%CF%8D%CF%82#Ancient_Greek "wikt:πούς") (_pous_, 'foot'), itself a variant form of [ὀκτάπους](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/%E1%BD%80%CE%BA%CF%84%CE%AC%CF%80%CE%BF%CF%85%CF%82#Ancient_Greek "wikt:ὀκτάπους"), a word used for example by [Alexander of Tralles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_of_Tralles "Alexander of Tralles") (c.525 – c.605).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Octopus#cite_note-etym-7)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Octopus#cite_note-8)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Octopus#cite_note-9)

The standard [pluralised](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plural "Plural") form of _octopus_ in English is _octopuses_;[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Octopus#cite_note-10) the Ancient Greek plural ὀκτώποδες, _octopodes_ (), has also been used historically.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Octopus#cite_note-OD-11) The alternative plural _octopi_ is usually considered etymologically incorrect, because it [wrongly assumes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hypercorrection "Hypercorrection") that _octopus_ is a Latin [second-declension](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_declension "Second declension")_[-us](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/-us#Latin "wikt:-us")_ noun or adjective when, in either Greek or Latin, it is a [third-declension](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Third_declension "Third declension") noun.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Octopus#cite_note-12)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Octopus#cite_note-13) Historically, the first plural to commonly appear in English language sources, in the early 19th century, is the Latinate form _octopi_,[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Octopus#cite_note-14) followed by the English form _octopuses_ in the latter half of the same century. The Hellenic plural is roughly contemporary in usage, although it is also the rarest.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Octopus#cite_note-15)

_[A Dictionary of Modern English Usage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Dictionary\_of\_Modern\_English\_Usage "A Dictionary of Modern English Usage")_ by H. W. Fowler states that the only acceptable plural in English is _octopuses_, that _octopi_ is misconceived, and _octopodes_[pedantic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pedantic "Pedantic");[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Octopus#cite_note-16)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Octopus#cite_note-17)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Octopus#cite_note-18) the last is nonetheless used frequently enough to be acknowledged by the [descriptivist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Descriptivist "Descriptivist")_Merriam-Webster 11th Collegiate Dictionary_ and _Webster's New World College Dictionary_.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Octopus#cite_note-19) The _[Oxford English Dictionary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oxford\_English\_Dictionary "Oxford English Dictionary")_ lists _octopuses_, _octopi_, and _octopodes_, in that order, reflecting frequency of use, calling _octopodes_ rare and noting that _octopi_ is based on a misunderstanding.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Octopus#cite_note-20) The _[New Oxford American Dictionary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New\_Oxford\_American\_Dictionary "New Oxford American Dictionary")_ (3rd Edition, 2010) lists _octopuses_ as the only acceptable pluralisation, and indicates that _octopodes_ is occasionally used, but that _octopi_ is incorrect.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Octopus#cite_note-NOAD-21)

## Anatomy and physiology

### Size

[](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:North_Pacific_Giant_Octopus.JPG)

A [giant Pacific octopus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giant_Pacific_octopus "Giant Pacific octopus") at Echizen Matsushima Aquarium, Japan

The [giant Pacific octopus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giant_Pacific_octopus "Giant Pacific octopus") (_Enteroctopus dofleini_) is often cited as the largest octopus species. Adults usually weigh 10–50 kg (22–110 lb), with an arm span of up to 4.8 m (16 ft).[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Octopus#cite_note-22) The largest specimen of this species to be scientifically documented reached a live mass of 71 kg (157 lb).[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Octopus#cite_note-23) Much larger sizes have been claimed:[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Octopus#cite_note-norman03-24) one specimen was recorded

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Have you ever felt like the things we think we know are actually a bit more mysterious than we give them credit for? Today we are diving deep into the intelligent invertebrate known as the octopus.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I was curious about the biology but also how they fit into human history. It seems like they have been around for a really long time.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That is fascinating. They first appear in scientific records during the Middle Jurassic period, yet humans have been talking about them for millennia.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Speaking of history, did you know they are sometimes called sea monsters in our myths? The kraken and the gorgons are all based on these creatures.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Exactly. Victor Hugo even wrote a battle against one in Toilers of the Sea, so they have always been part of the cultural imagination.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: But beyond the stories, the science is wild. Most people think of them as soft blobs, but they are actually some of the smartest animals on the planet.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That is what I wanted to highlight. They possess over five hundred million neurons, a number comparable to a domestic dog.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Really? So their intelligence is down right there with mammals despite lacking a backbone?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Precisely. In fact, two-thirds of their neurons are located in the arms themselves, allowing them to act almost independently.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That is insane. If I touch a wall with my arm while sleeping, my arm knows it collided with a wall.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: It does. The suckers on their arms have chemoreceptors, meaning they can taste what they touch before they even grab it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Imagine trying to eat something without knowing if it is edible or toxic until you grab it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Exactly. And their movement is equally bizarre. They trail their appendages backward as they swim using a water jet.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So they are basically biological water jets. They can also change color rapidly to blend into the coral reefs.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They can even hide by changing the pattern on their skin to look like a piece of rock or seagrass.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And they defend themselves by squirting ink. It is a thick, dark blob made mostly of the pigment melanin.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes, to confuse predators while they escape. But not all octopuses are safe to touch, particularly the blue-ringed variety.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I have heard they are deadly. Only the blue-ringed ones are known to be lethal to humans though.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: True, but all octopuses are venomous, so you do not want to get close to any of them unnecessarily.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Their life cycle is also quite tragic. The males usually die shortly after mating, depositing sperm in the female.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And the females then care for the eggs until they hatch, only to die shortly after, which makes them very short-lived.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And the female can lay hundreds of thousands of eggs in a single clutch.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes, up to five hundred thousand for some species, and they brood them for five months in some cases.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It is a fascinating story of life, death, and evolution. Octopuses really challenge what we think about intelligence.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They are truly a marvel of nature, blending the ancient with the incredibly modern in their capabilities.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So if you ever see one, respect it and stay away from the blue-ringed ones.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Agreed. Until next time, I am Sara and this is George discussing the mysteries of the deep sea.
